heading: What a native service reaches
body: Native services use their platform SDK (software development kit). They inject an ApplicationEventPublisher for local events that they own. They use OnEvent, and OnStart and OnStop for the lifecycle. Each example initializes the service and publishes a CatalogCount model. A listener updates the count, and cleanup resets it. Old callbacks from an earlier activation cannot change the owners that replaced it. A native service has no page, so it cannot use Tachyon's browser APIs (such as `Clock`, `Clipboard` or `Geolocation`) or listen for their built-in event models (such as `ConnectivityChanged`). The build refuses them in a service that is linked into the app (`TY1317`). Use them in a JavaScript, TypeScript or WebAssembly service, and send the result to the native service with an event. `WindowControls` is the one exception: a linked service gets it from the host through an uninitialized `WindowControls` field with `Needs` or `NeedsAll` (ADR 0089; see the feature "What a page may do to its window"). Only Swift, Kotlin, C# and Rust services are linked into a native app. JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Go, Ruby, Java, F#, Lua and Python services always run in the page, also inside a native app, so this section has no tab for them.
